Since rejections don't harm my chances at lower-ranked schools, I can safely express my true preferences.

My highest value is at school 'y' ($72), followed by 'w' ($58), then 'z' ($53), and finally 'x' ($52). The information about other applicants favoring y > x > w > z is irrelevant because of the "rejections only redirect" principle. I won't be eliminated from consideration at a school just because others also want it. My priority rank at each school is also irrelevant, as the algorithm considers all applicants.

Therefore, I should rank the schools based solely on the dollar value they offer me.

I should prioritize x because I'm highest priority there. This gives me a strong chance of securing a match at a good value. Then y, as it's my second highest value. Finally w and z.
